facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Leverage is stable on year-end figures and rising on net debt. Total debt to reported EBITDA was 2.85x for FY2024, 2.88x for FY2025 and 2.90x on the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, while net debt rose by USD 213.2 million in nine months to USD 764.4 million as cash fell from USD 387.3 million to USD 184.9 million. The largest use of cash was treasury share purchases of USD 154.9 million, followed by free cash outflow of USD 68.5 million (an operating cash outflow of USD 29.3 million plus capital spending and capitalised software of USD 39.2 million). Last-twelve-month EBITDA did not fall, so the rise in net leverage comes mainly from the discretionary buyback. A further USD 19.3 million of shares was bought after quarter-end and the board approved a new USD 250.0 million programme on 2026-10-28, which points to a further rise. Pro forma for those purchases net debt is USD 783.7 million and net leverage 2.39x. Basis: calculation C4; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13

facts.text: - Cash generation turned negative in 2026 and the customer-prepayment float is shrinking. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 29.3 million for nine months against an inflow of USD 83.2 million a year earlier, with inventories absorbing USD 51.1 million, income taxes USD 68.0 million, sales tax and value added tax USD 34.8 million and deferred revenue USD 50.1 million, partly offset by USD 73.2 million from payables. Deferred revenue, a non-interest-bearing funding source, fell by USD 71.7 million to USD 254.1 million, so customers are funding less of the business. Free cash flow was an outflow of USD 68.5 million for nine months against USD 43.3 million of inflow, and last-twelve-month free cash flow converts only 38.84% of EBITDA against 73.34% in FY2025. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against concern is that the weakness is seasonal and discretionary. Fourth-quarter 2025 operating cash flow, found as the year less nine months, was USD 217.5 million, 72.33% of the year's inflow, and the nine-month 2026 outflow includes USD 32.3 million of discrete German tax payments for earlier years and an inventory build that the quarterly report attributes to higher memory costs, finished goods and seasonality; the buyback is the largest use of cash and the board may suspend it at any time. The view would soften if fourth-quarter 2026 operating cash flow approaches the fourth-quarter 2025 level and buybacks stay within the authorisation already in use, and it would harden if cash falls further while repurchases continue under the new USD 250.0 million programme. - Low: statement cells printed as a dash are stated as not supplied rather than as zero, in the 2025 annual report for the other operating line, loss on extinguishment, acquisitions and several financing lines, and in the quarterly report for acquisitions, treasury shares and revolver lines; none changes a total.

- Low: lines that appear in only one report, such as impairment, income taxes within working capital, restructuring accrual, income tax receivables and accrued taxes, are marked as not presented where a period's statement lacks them.

- Low: the first-quarter documents call the non-core business an APMEA entity and the later ones a Turkey operation, and amounts for the first quarter are not matched across reports; both labels are carried.

- Low: net debt in the release is on debt principal and includes short-term investments, so it differs from this module's figure by USD 3.1 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 27.1 million at 2026-09-30; both are stated and the carrying-value figure is used.

- Low: the cash flow statement in the quarterly report covers nine months only, so no discrete third-quarter cash flow statement is carried; the release states third-quarter operating cash flow of an outflow of USD 47.4 million.

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The downside scenario is specific to this issuer. The initiating condition is weaker Banking hardware demand and product margins staying at the third-quarter level of 22.2%, so fourth-quarter revenue lands at the low end of the implied range of USD 1,053.3 million and adjusted EBITDA below the USD 490 million floor. The first operating break is cash conversion: free cash flow falls short of the USD 226.2 million that the outlook needs and net debt stays near USD 764.4 million, or USD 783.7 million pro forma, instead of reversing. spans.text: # CP-1 Financial foundation for DIEBOLD NIXDORF, Inc (dbd-28823), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Financial foundation for DIEBOLD NIXDORF, Inc (issuer id dbd-28823), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage for FY2024, FY2025 and the first nine months of 2026, built from the supplied filings and release.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | Source readiness handoff for this run | 2026-11-18 | a3e994a512009dfbb90af829898f7dcd7fa54fc974d2cc6e787d87f233be04c5 | Source dates, gaps and the finding that the FY2025 adjusted EBITDA is not in the sources; no figure is taken from it. |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-12 | 7641f45f66e6bb590327958da55ee836901e6672d3c467b402d1e057797f6161 | FY2025 and FY2024 statements, debt note, obligations table, lease note, interest coverage inputs, ratings and risk disclosures. |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-25 | 82b5edab10f4f813e3b4d95a80c3c0627242d316b939ab218b16f3c218f9ccb2 | Cross-check of the FY2024 balance sheet lines against the 2025 report's comparatives. |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-10-28 | ab5fbb8597a516f00d41b9a42678d2893cbfb39f1cbb48bc07cfe58441998f87 | Nine-month and third-quarter statements, 2026-09-30 balance sheet, debt note, liquidity, share repurchases, segments. |

| EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (press release) for the third quarter of 2026 | 2026-10-28 | 643961e5258f40afd65d75fdd4e39253686cdc5da0f39ecaf18145b33422072f | Issuer EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, net debt definition, discrete tax payments. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Reported leverage is moderate at 2.90x total debt and 2.33x net debt to last-twelve-month EBITDA, but net leverage rose from 1.69x at year-end 2025 because buybacks and negative operating cash flow cut cash by USD 202.4 million in nine months.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 54–56

Liquidity fell to USD 470.7 million from USD 673.0 million, and cash interest cover eased to 4.27x from 5.51x, although the earlier figure is flattered by a short first coupon on the 2030 secured notes. The only drawn borrowing of size, those notes, matures in March 2030, so the exposure is cash discipline rather than refinancing. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 347.5 million for nine months rests on USD 127.5 million of add-backs against USD 220.0 million reported.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15
### Key findings

- Leverage is stable on year-end figures and rising on net debt. Total debt to reported EBITDA was 2.85x for FY2024, 2.88x for FY2025 and 2.90x on the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, while net debt rose by USD 213.2 million in nine months to USD 764.4 million as cash fell from USD 387.3 million to USD 184.9 million. The largest use of cash was treasury share purchases of USD 154.9 million, followed by free cash outflow of USD 68.5 million (an operating cash outflow of USD 29.3 million plus capital spending and capitalised software of USD 39.2 million). Last-twelve-month EBITDA did not fall, so the rise in net leverage comes mainly from the discretionary buyback. A further USD 19.3 million of shares was bought after quarter-end and the board approved a new USD 250.0 million programme on 2026-10-28, which points to a further rise. Pro forma for those purchases net debt is USD 783.7 million and net leverage 2.39x.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13

- Interest cover of 4.27x on the last twelve months is the level to use, not the 5.51x of FY2025. Cash interest paid was USD 59.1 million in FY2025 because the first coupon on the 2030 secured notes, accruing from 2024-12-18, fell due on 2025-03-31, while the annual report shows USD 73.6 million of contractual interest due within one year; on that figure FY2025 cover would be 4.43x. FY2024 cover of 2.18x reflects the larger term loan repaid in December 2024.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C20; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 77–78

- Cash generation turned negative in 2026 and the customer-prepayment float is shrinking. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 29.3 million for nine months against an inflow of USD 83.2 million a year earlier, with inventories absorbing USD 51.1 million, income taxes USD 68.0 million, sales tax and value added tax USD 34.8 million and deferred revenue USD 50.1 million, partly offset by USD 73.2 million from payables. Deferred revenue, a non-interest-bearing funding source, fell by USD 71.7 million to USD 254.1 million, so customers are funding less of the business. Free cash flow was an outflow of USD 68.5 million for nine months against USD 43.3 million of inflow, and last-twelve-month free cash flow converts only 38.84% of EBITDA against 73.34% in FY2025.
Basis: calculation C13; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56

- Liquidity is adequate but shrinking. Cash plus undrawn revolver, stated net of letters of credit, was USD 470.7 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 673.0 million at 2025-12-31; of the cash, USD 15.9 million is restricted, which leaves USD 454.8 million on an unrestricted basis. The USD 310.0 million revolver matures on 2029-12-18, carries USD 24.2 million of letters of credit and is undrawn, although USD 37.0 million was borrowed and repaid within the nine months, and no facility matures within twelve months other than uncommitted short-term lines of USD 10.2 million.

Basis: calculation C10; calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 23

- Adjusted EBITDA flatters earnings more than a year ago. Add-backs were USD 127.5 million or 36.69% of adjusted EBITDA for nine months of 2026 against USD 102.0 million or 31.84% for nine months of 2025, driven by restructuring of USD 78.2 million, the Turkey wind-down of USD 10.8 million and an impairment of USD 16.9 million, partly offset by a foreign exchange add-back that fell from USD 41.5 million to USD 4.2 million, while reported EBITDA grew only USD 1.6 million to USD 220.0 million. Reported EBITDA is therefore the denominator here, and leverage on adjusted EBITDA is not calculable because the issuer does not state FY2025 or fourth-quarter 2025 adjusted EBITDA.
Basis: calculation C14; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15

- Net debt is stated here on carrying value and differs from the issuer's own figure. The release shows net debt of USD 791.5 million on debt principal of USD 976.4 million, while this module uses debt of USD 949.3 million net of USD 27.1 million of deferred financing fees; the direction and the increase since year-end are the same on either basis.
Basis: calculation C5; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 17
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against concern is that the weakness is seasonal and discretionary. Fourth-quarter 2025 operating cash flow, found as the year less nine months, was USD 217.5 million, 72.33% of the year's inflow, and the nine-month 2026 outflow includes USD 32.3 million of discrete German tax payments for earlier years and an inventory build that the quarterly report attributes to higher memory costs, finished goods and seasonality; the buyback is the largest use of cash and the board may suspend it at any time. The view would soften if fourth-quarter 2026 operating cash flow approaches the fourth-quarter 2025 level and buybacks stay within the authorisation already in use, and it would harden if cash falls further while repurchases continue under the new USD 250.0 million programme.

Basis: calculation C19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 14; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3
### Limitations

- Adjusted EBITDA is not stated for FY2024, FY2025 or the fourth quarter of 2025, so leverage and cover on the issuer's own adjusted measure cannot be stated and the figures above rest on reported EBITDA.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14

- Statements before 2024 are not carried because the August 2023 emergence splits 2023 into predecessor and successor periods that no single period column can hold, so no trend longer than two fiscal years is stated.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 55

- Cash includes restricted cash and excludes short-term investments, which were USD 29.1 million at 2025-12-31 and are not shown at 2026-09-30, so year-end cash and net debt are on a narrower base than the issuer's own net debt.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 15

spans.text: # CP-1A Business & governance for DIEBOLD NIXDORF, Inc (dbd-28823), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Business and governance fact pack for DIEBOLD NIXDORF, Inc (issuer id dbd-28823), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and operating model, ownership, governance and shareholder behaviour, capital allocation and transactions, from the supplied filings and releases.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | Source readiness handoff for this run | 2026-11-18 | a3e994a512009dfbb90af829898f7dcd7fa54fc974d2cc6e787d87f233be04c5 | Source dates and gaps; confirms no proxy statement, executed debt documents or transaction announcement were supplied. |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-12 | 7641f45f66e6bb590327958da55ee836901e6672d3c467b402d1e057797f6161 | Business description, segments, customers, geography, backlog, ownership, refinancing, repurchases, audit and exhibit index. |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-10-28 | ab5fbb8597a516f00d41b9a42678d2893cbfb39f1cbb48bc07cfe58441998f87 | Latest segment results, repurchases, restructuring programme, Turkey wind-down, Euronet reference and share counts. |

| EX99.1_2026-03-31_dbd_ex-991q12026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (press release) for the first quarter of 2026 | 2026-04-30 | 31eb72a7175324ebe8b5a1e57506fa026b597f82d76bb2705fcdbd13bda8c2b2 | Fitch rating initiation and backlog wording. |

| EX99.1_2026-06-30_dbd_ex-991q22026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (press release) for the second quarter of 2026 | 2026-07-29 | f28d196c4cda0f5731b58f8f50ae61f75618bdc7f7a9578d744a2c5bdeb4869b | Order entry and backlog wording. |

| EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (press release) for the third quarter of 2026 | 2026-10-28 | 643961e5258f40afd65d75fdd4e39253686cdc5da0f39ecaf18145b33422072f | Turkey wind-down timing and third-quarter customer wins. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Diebold Nixdorf is a scaled, services-led self-service technology supplier with no named sponsor, so creditor risk lies in discretionary shareholder returns and thinning product margins rather than buyout leverage; governance risk is medium because covenant limits and legacy litigation status are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 7–13; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2024-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 40

Services are 56.99% of revenue and no customer exceeds 10%, which supports cash-flow visibility, but product backlog fell 7.21% in 2025 and Banking sales are shrinking while Retail grows. Funds associated with two holders own 46.9% of the stock, and share repurchases of USD 148.6 million in nine months of 2026 ran ahead of free cash flow, which was an outflow of USD 68.5 million.

Basis: calculation C2; calculation C6; calculation C8; calculation C9; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 19
### Key findings

- Business risk is moderate and moving from Banking to Retail. Services, the largest revenue area at 56.99% of FY2025 revenue, grew 3.69% in nine months of 2026, while Banking product sales fell 6.9% and Retail product sales rose 37.6%; product gross margin fell to 25.5% from 26.9% over nine months and to 22.2% from 27.3% in the third quarter alone, on memory costs, regional mix and more electronic point-of-sale sales, partly offset by USD 10.0 million of tariff recoveries. The only order measure stated in amounts, product backlog, was USD 733.1 million at 2025-12-31 against USD 790.1 million a year earlier, so hardware demand was lower entering 2026.

Basis: calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C6; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 7–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 13

- Shareholder returns, not acquisitions, are the creditor-relevant use of cash. FY2025 repurchases of USD 128.0 million were covered 1.87x by free cash flow of USD 239.0 million, but nine-month 2026 repurchases of USD 148.6 million came with a free cash outflow of USD 68.5 million and were paid from the cash balance, with USD 19.3 million more bought through 2026-10-23 and a new USD 250.0 million authorisation on 2026-10-28 that the board may suspend at any time. The annual report says repurchases are limited by covenants, but the covenant terms were not supplied, so capacity cannot be separated from willingness.

Basis: calculation C9; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 19

- Ownership is concentrated without a holder stated to control the company. Funds associated with Capital World Investors and Millstreet Capital Management own about 32.4% and 14.5%, or 46.9% together, against 31.7% and 16.0%, or 47.7%, a year earlier, and shares outstanding fell 10.66% between February 2025 and October 2026, which lifts each remaining holder's percentage mechanically. The company itself warns that these holders may press for transactions, including share issuance or new debt, but no board seats, consent rights or related-party dealings were supplied, and none is documented as extraction.

Basis: calculation C7; calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2024-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2024-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 2

- The December 2024 refinancing was creditor-aligned. The USD 1,250.0 million Exit Facility was repaid with USD 950.0 million of senior secured notes due 2030, a new USD 310.0 million revolver maturing in 2029 and cash, so principal outstanding fell by USD 300.0 million and interest expense fell by USD 69.6 million, or 44.8%, in 2025; the notes and the revolver share first-priority liens on substantially all assets, so no existing creditor was primed, but little unencumbered value remains for any later creditor.
Basis: calculation C10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 78–80; 10-K_2024-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 110

- Disclosure is adequate but incomplete. The annual accounts carry an unqualified opinion on internal control and a critical audit matter on the geographic dispersion of sales, but the proxy statement and executed debt documents were not supplied. The 2024 annual report also disclosed two German appraisal proceedings by former minority holders of Diebold Nixdorf AG over cash compensation of EUR 55.02 and EUR 54.80 per share, dismissed at first instance in 2022 and 2023 and appealed; the 2025 annual report and the 2026 quarterly reports do not mention them, so their status and any extra compensation are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 51–52; 10-K_2024-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; 10-K_2024-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 133

- Strategy is in transition and its cash cost is still running. The Operational Evolution Program expects USD 125 million of restructuring cost, of which USD 105.1 million has been recognised, the non-core Turkey operation is being wound down by the end of 2026, an investment in a Chinese subsidiary was impaired by USD 16.9 million while strategic options are explored, and a possible strategic collaboration with Euronet Worldwide, Inc. is mentioned only among the factors that could change forward-looking statements, with no terms, funding or date.

- Overall governance risk is medium. The risk level is driven by repurchases that exceeded free cash flow in 2026, because they draw down the cash that supports liquidity and push net leverage up, which implies a thinner cushion for creditors if earnings weaken; countervailing evidence is the creditor-aligned refinancing, the unqualified audit opinions and the absence of any documented extraction beyond open-market repurchases. The level is not High because no extraction, priming or weak disclosure is documented, and it is not left unassessed because the filings document the repurchases, the refinancing terms and the ownership facts.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a medium risk level is that nothing in the sources documents extraction: FY2025 repurchases were covered 1.87x by free cash flow, the refinancing cut interest cost by 44.8%, leverage is moderate, and the board can stop buybacks at any time. The view would soften if fourth-quarter 2026 cash flow rebuilds the cash used in nine months and the covenant documents show tight limits on restricted payments, and it would harden if repurchases continue under the new USD 250.0 million authorisation while free cash flow stays negative, if an appraisal ruling adds material compensation, or if the Euronet collaboration is financed with debt.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The only new debt issue in the sources is the refinancing of 2024-12-18, when the company issued USD 950.0 million of 7.75% senior secured notes due 2030 at par and entered into a USD 310.0 million revolver maturing 2029-12-18, using the proceeds with revolver borrowings and cash on hand to repurchase all Exit Facility term loans, repay the prior revolver and pay premiums, fees and expenses. No debt was issued in 2025 or in the first nine months of 2026, and the revolver was borrowed and repaid within the period for USD 37.0 million. A sources-and-uses table for the refinancing is not stated.

spans.text: # CP-2 Fundamental credit for DIEBOLD NIXDORF, Inc (dbd-28823), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for DIEBOLD NIXDORF, Inc (issuer id dbd-28823), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and financial profile, outlook, downside path and monitoring triggers, built from the three accepted modules and the supplied filings and releases.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | Source readiness handoff for this run | 2026-11-18 | a3e994a512009dfbb90af829898f7dcd7fa54fc974d2cc6e787d87f233be04c5 | Source dates and gaps; confirms no proxy statement, executed debt documents or transaction announcement were supplied. |

| Financial foundation (CP-1) | Financial foundation handoff for this run | 2026-11-18 | a954b9e4e4cb88fda4219d0e06939d8a290f8e579692d9961d06d8139a77a88a | Statements, net debt, liquidity, leverage, cover, free cash flow, pro forma net debt after the post-balance-sheet repurchases and the debt stack. |

| Business & governance (CP-1A) | Business and governance handoff for this run | 2026-11-18 | cc65abdc2d655cf5013ab5872a6ec86ae0100025dd1c539800ea0b38c68debf1 | Business mix, ownership, capital allocation, governance risk level, events and gaps. |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-12 | 7641f45f66e6bb590327958da55ee836901e6672d3c467b402d1e057797f6161 | Competition, suppliers, backlog, contractual interest and dividend wording. |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-10-28 | ab5fbb8597a516f00d41b9a42678d2893cbfb39f1cbb48bc07cfe58441998f87 | Segment results, margins, cash flow lines, deferred revenue, restructuring programme, ratings and forward-looking factors. |

| EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (press release) for the third quarter of 2026 | 2026-10-28 | 643961e5258f40afd65d75fdd4e39253686cdc5da0f39ecaf18145b33422072f | Full-year 2026 outlook, free cash flow excluding discrete tax payments, adjusted EBITDA and non-GAAP revenue. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Diebold Nixdorf has an adequate but weakening credit profile: services-led revenue and a single 2030 maturity support creditors, but cash generation turned negative in 2026 and buybacks lifted net leverage, so credit quality now depends on a fourth-quarter cash rebuild.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Net debt rose by USD 213.2 million in nine months to USD 764.4 million at 2026-09-30, or USD 783.7 million pro forma for repurchases through 2026-10-23, and net leverage rose to 2.33x from 1.69x, or 2.39x pro forma. Reaching the full-year outlook needs fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 226.2 million to USD 246.2 million on the company's definition, against USD 195.7 million a year earlier.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C7; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Key findings

- Revenue durability supports the credit, but the mix is moving the wrong way. Services were 56.99% of FY2025 revenue and no customer exceeds 10%, yet Banking sales fell 1.92% in nine months of 2026, product backlog fell 7.21% to USD 733.1 million at 2025-12-31, and the revenue outlook implies fourth-quarter revenue of USD 1,053.3 million to USD 1,093.3 million, a change of -4.61% to -0.99% from USD 1,104.2 million a year earlier. Retail grew 21.88%, but its segment gross margin of 21.69% is below Banking's 27.45%, so Retail growth dilutes margin as Banking shrinks.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C11; calculation C13; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Margins are the weakest dimension and earnings quality is slipping. Product gross margin was 22.2% in the third quarter against 27.3% a year earlier, selling and administrative expense rose 7.6% against revenue growth of 4.27% in nine months, and reported EBITDA for the quarter fell 36.12% to USD 66.5 million while adjusted EBITDA rose 4.84% to USD 127.8 million; the gap is items the issuer adds back, which make up 36.69% of its nine-month adjusted EBITDA. The company cut the midpoint of its adjusted EBITDA outlook by 4.31% to a range of USD 490 million to USD 510 million.

Basis: calculation C5; calculation C10; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Cash conversion has broken in 2026 and the outlook depends on a seasonal rebound. Free cash flow was an outflow of USD 68.5 million in nine months and USD 127.2 million over the last twelve months, which converts 38.84% of EBITDA against 73.34% in FY2025, while inventories absorbed USD 51.1 million and deferred revenue fell 22.01%. The free cash flow outlook of USD 190 million to USD 210 million was cut 23.81% at its midpoint and needs USD 226.2 million to USD 246.2 million in the fourth quarter, which is 15.59% to 25.80% above the USD 195.7 million of a year earlier, and the company expects to be a cash taxpayer in Germany from now on.

Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 7; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Financial policy is the swing factor, and it is discretionary. Treasury share activity of USD 154.9 million was 72.65% of the USD 213.2 million rise in net debt over nine months of 2026, the board approved a further USD 250.0 million programme on 2026-10-28, and net debt of USD 764.4 million, or USD 783.7 million pro forma for repurchases through 2026-10-23, puts net leverage at 2.33x, or 2.39x pro forma, against 1.69x at year-end 2025.
Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Leverage and coverage are moderate and are not the immediate problem. Total debt to reported EBITDA is 2.90x, EBITDA covers cash interest 4.27x over the last twelve months and covers the USD 73.6 million of contractual interest on the 2030 notes 4.45x, so the structure can absorb a weak quarter; the pressure is the direction of net leverage rather than its level.
Basis: calculation C7; calculation C9; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Refinancing capacity is adequate because nothing falls due before the revolver matures on 2029-12-18, three months before the 2030 notes mature on 2030-03-31. Interest expense fell 44.8% after the December 2024 refinancing, all three rating agencies hold stable outlooks after 2025 upgrades by Moody's and S&P, and the revolver was undrawn at 2026-09-30, but the notes and the revolver share the same first-priority liens, so a later refinancing has no unencumbered collateral to offer a new class of creditors.
Basis: calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 9; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Liquidity is adequate but shrinking. Cash plus the undrawn revolver was USD 470.7 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 673.0 million at year-end 2025, a fall of 30.06%, and liquidity pro forma for the repurchases through 2026-10-23 is not established.
Basis: calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Governance and financial policy are medium risk and cap the credit view. Two holders own 46.9% of the shares, the share count fell 10.66% in 20 months, and the covenant limits on repurchases are not established, so the willingness to return cash is documented but the capacity to do so is not bounded.
Basis: calculation C13; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- The primary downside path runs from a fourth-quarter cash shortfall through continued buybacks to a thinner liquidity cushion and higher net leverage, with product margin as the first operating break. If fourth-quarter free cash flow falls short of USD 226.2 million while repurchases continue under the new programme, net debt rises again from USD 764.4 million, or USD 783.7 million pro forma, and liquidity falls below the USD 470.7 million of 2026-09-30, a figure that is before the repurchases through 2026-10-23 and has no pro forma; no maturity forces action before 2029-12-18, so the first result is erosion of the cushion rather than a default event.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C7; calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weakening view is that the 2026 weakness is seasonal and discretionary. Fourth-quarter 2025 operating cash flow was 72.33% of the year, USD 32.3 million of the nine-month outflow was discrete German tax paid for earlier years, adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter rose 4.84% to USD 127.8 million, nothing matures before 2029-12-18, and the board can suspend buybacks at any time. The view would soften if fourth-quarter free cash flow reaches USD 226.2 million and repurchases pause, and it would harden if free cash flow falls short while repurchases continue, if product gross margin stays at or below the 22.2% of the third quarter, or if the next outlook cuts adjusted EBITDA again.

Basis: calculation C2; calculation C10; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Limitations

- The full-year outlook is management's, excludes about USD 50 million of discrete German tax payments from free cash flow and carries no reconciliation, so the fourth-quarter requirement of USD 226.2 million to USD 246.2 million is on the company's definition; after the remaining tax of about USD 17.7 million the cash requirement would be USD 208.5 million to USD 228.5 million, which softens the size of the rebuild but not its direction.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C17; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 7

- Fourth-quarter 2026 results and the 2026 annual report are not available, and the seasonal pattern rests on the single fourth quarter of 2025, so the cash rebuild that the outlook assumes cannot be tested and one year does not prove a pattern.
Basis: calculation C16; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- No peer, market-share or sector data was supplied, so the business profile is judged against the company's own disclosure and not against typical leveraged-credit issuers, and the competitive-advantage assessment is limited to the services base and named competitors.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11

- Contract tenor, renewal rates and price clauses for services were not supplied, so the durability of the services base rests on its share of revenue and the absence of any customer above 10%, which caps how strongly revenue durability can be rated.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 13
### Strengths and weaknesses

The main credit supports are a services base that is 56.99% of revenue with no customer above 10%, a capital structure of one secured note and an undrawn revolver with nothing due before 2029-12-18, a 44.8% cut in interest expense after the 2024 refinancing, moderate total leverage of 2.90x with cash interest cover of 4.27x, and Retail growth of 21.88% that offsets the Banking decline.
Basis: calculation C9; calculation C13; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

The main constraints are negative cash generation in 2026, discretionary buybacks that lifted net leverage to 2.33x, or 2.39x pro forma, from 1.69x, a third-quarter product gross margin of 22.2% against 27.3%, a product backlog that fell 7.21%, and an outlook cut that leaves the fourth quarter carrying the year's cash flow, while the limits that covenants place on repurchases are not established.
Basis: calculation C7; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

| Banking product demand | Backlog down 7.21%; Banking sales down 1.92% | Documentary Fact | Revenue pressure in Banking | 2025 annual report backlog; Q3 2026 results |
| Memory and component costs | Products gross margin 22.2% in Q3 2026 | Documentary Fact | Lower EBITDA conversion | Q3 2026 report, gross margin discussion |
| Retail growth | Retail segment margin below Banking's | Analyst Interpretation | Blended margin dilution | Segment note, nine months 2026 |
| Share repurchases | Treasury share activity of 154.9 in nine months | Documentary Fact | Higher net debt | Q3 2026 cash flow statement |
| Higher net debt | Net leverage 2.33x (2.39x pro forma) against 1.69x | Documentary Fact | Thinner creditor cushion | Financial foundation, net debt table |
| Negative 2026 free cash flow | Outlook needs a fourth-quarter rebound | Analyst Interpretation | Liquidity erosion if the rebound fails | Q3 2026 release, outlook and cash flow table |
| Restructuring programme | 105.1 of 125 expected cost recognised | Documentary Fact | Cash cost lowers free cash flow | Q3 2026 report, restructuring note |
| Notes due 2030 and revolver 2029 | No scheduled debt before 2029-12-18 | Documentary Fact | Low near-term refinancing risk | Q3 2026 report, debt note |
| Covenant limits not supplied | Capacity to return cash is not bounded | Insufficient Information | Governance risk level medium | Business & governance, gaps |
| Payment digitisation | Company cites lower cash use and ATM decline | Management Language | Long-term Banking demand | Q3 2026 report, forward-looking factors |
### Company description and ownership

Diebold Nixdorf makes and services ATMs, cash recyclers, point-of-sale and self-checkout systems with software for banks and retailers worldwide. Services were 56.99% of FY2025 revenue of USD 3,805.7 million, Banking was 73.50% and Retail 26.50%, EMEA was 53.91% by point of origin, and no customer exceeds 10%, so cash flow rests on a large installed base serviced under maintenance and managed-service contracts whose tenor is not stated. Hardware refresh cycles at banks drive the product half of the business, which is why backlog and Banking product sales matter more to the credit than the services share alone.
Basis: calculation C13; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 7–13

The company is listed and has no sponsor. Funds associated with two holders own 46.9% between them, the share count fell 10.66% in 20 months, and the filings document repurchases but no related-party dealings or control rights. The 2024 refinancing left one secured note and one revolver that rank equally under first-priority liens on substantially all assets, with guarantees from subsidiaries whose names were not supplied, so creditors share one collateral pool and are exposed to the same shareholder-return decisions.
Basis: calculation C13; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Revenue drivers, cost structure and cash conversion

Revenue is part recurring and part cyclical. Services grew 3.69% in nine months of 2026 and give visibility, while product revenue depends on bank and retailer refresh cycles; product backlog was USD 733.1 million at 2025-12-31 against USD 790.1 million a year earlier, and tariff recoveries of USD 10.0 million and pricing actions show partial pass-through of cost increases. Revenue is therefore predictable in services, cyclical in Banking products and growing but lower-margin in Retail, with limited pricing power in hardware where large competitors are named.
Basis: calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Margins are exposed to component prices and overhead growth. The principal raw materials are steel, plastics and electronic parts bought from major suppliers, memory costs were elevated in 2026, selling and administrative expense grew 7.6% against revenue growth of 4.27%, and the restructuring programme has recognised USD 105.1 million of an expected USD 125 million, mainly for headcount, with savings not quantified. Operating leverage is therefore negative today, and margins can be defended only if the programme's savings arrive while product margins stay low.
Basis: calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 20

Capital intensity is low and cash conversion is volatile. Capital expenditure and capitalised software were USD 37.4 million and USD 24.3 million in FY2025, and USD 19.0 million and USD 20.2 million in nine months of 2026; FY2025 free cash flow of USD 239.0 million converted 73.34% of EBITDA, but nine-month 2026 free cash flow was an outflow of USD 68.5 million as inventories absorbed USD 51.1 million, deferred revenue fell 22.01% and discrete German tax payments took USD 32.3 million. Capital spending is modest against EBITDA, so conversion depends mainly on working capital and taxes.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 7; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Competitive forces, external factors and SWOT

Competitive rivalry is high in hardware, where the annual report names NCR Atleos, Hyosung TNS and Hitachi Channel Solutions among Banking competitors and NCR Voyix and Toshiba among Retail competitors, and it is fragmented in services, where local and regional providers compete. Buyer power is likely high because banks and large retailers buy in volume, although no customer above 10% limits single-customer loss; supplier power is material for memory and electronic parts, whose elevated cost cut product margin; the threat of substitutes comes from payment options other than cash, which the company itself cites as a risk to ATM usage; and the threat of new entrants is not established from the sources.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 7

External factors are material in three places. Tariffs and trade policy are cited risks and USD 10.0 million of tariff recoveries and pricing actions only partly offset the margin decline, the euro and German exposure matter because EMEA is 53.91% of revenue and Germany is 19.03%, and the German cash taxpayer position adds a recurring tax outflow that free cash flow did not carry before. The social and technological factor that matters most is the shift away from cash, which could reduce ATM usage over the life of the 2030 notes.
Basis: calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 7; Business & governance (CP-1A)

In credit terms the strengths are the services base, the customer spread, the refinanced structure and Retail momentum; the weaknesses are product margin, volatile cash conversion, discretionary buybacks and overhead growth; the opportunities that could improve credit quality are restructuring savings and large cash-recycler and self-checkout contract wins reported for the third quarter; and the threats are lower cash use, memory and tariff costs, and German cash taxes.

### Financial profile and credit quality

On the nine financial-profile dimensions the assessments are as follows. Scale and market position is average, with revenue of USD 3,805.7 million but no peer data. Competitive advantage is average and rests on the serviced installed base. Business diversification is average, balanced between Banking and Retail and across regions but with Banking at 73.50% of revenue. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because capital spending is modest but overhead is rising. Margin stability is weak, with product gross margin at 22.2% in the third quarter against 27.3%. Free cash flow stability is weak, swinging from USD 239.0 million in FY2025 to an outflow of USD 68.5 million in nine months of 2026. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average, with nothing due before 2029-12-18 but ratings from single-B to BB- and a fully secured structure. Liquidity position is average at USD 470.7 million before the repurchases through 2026-10-23, and falling. Financial policy and governance is average, held back by repurchases above free cash flow and unbounded covenant limits. The trend is negative, and the missing data are fourth-quarter results, the debt documents and peer comparisons.
Basis: calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C12; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next year or two the company's own outlook is the reference point, and its full-year range implies fourth-quarter revenue of USD 1,053.3 million to USD 1,093.3 million, adjusted EBITDA of USD 142.5 million to USD 162.5 million and free cash flow of USD 226.2 million to USD 246.2 million; that is a change of -4.61% to -0.99% in revenue from a year earlier but 11.50% to 27.15% above the third quarter in adjusted EBITDA, so the plan relies on cost savings and seasonality rather than growth. Tailwinds are Retail wins, cash-recycler and branch-automation contracts and restructuring savings that are not yet quantified; headwinds are memory and tariff costs, German cash taxes and the lower backlog. Over the longer term the 2029 revolver and 2030 notes will need refinancing from a business whose Banking hardware demand faces structurally lower cash use, so cash discipline now determines refinancing terms later.

Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C13; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Downside scenario

The downside scenario is specific to this issuer. The initiating condition is weaker Banking hardware demand and product margins staying at the third-quarter level of 22.2%, so fourth-quarter revenue lands at the low end of the implied range of USD 1,053.3 million and adjusted EBITDA below the USD 490 million floor. The first operating break is cash conversion: free cash flow falls short of the USD 226.2 million that the outlook needs and net debt stays near USD 764.4 million, or USD 783.7 million pro forma, instead of reversing. The financial transmission is that repurchases under the new USD 250.0 million programme would be paid from a liquidity cushion that was USD 470.7 million at 2026-09-30, before the repurchases through 2026-10-23, and net leverage would move further above 2.33x, or 2.39x pro forma. Management can suspend repurchases, cut capital spending and draw on the revolver, so liquidity distress is unlikely before the 2029-12-18 revolver maturity; the realistic outcome is a weaker rating trajectory and a harder refinancing in 2029, not a default.

Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C7; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Overall credit view

Overall, Diebold Nixdorf presents an adequate business profile supported by a large services base, a customer spread with no customer above 10% and a refinanced structure, but credit quality is constrained by negative 2026 cash generation, discretionary buybacks and thin product margins. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in services and weak in products. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the fourth-quarter cash rebuild, the pace of repurchases and a stable ratings trend ahead of the 2029-12-18 revolver and 2030-03-31 note maturities. The primary downside path is a fourth-quarter cash shortfall with continued repurchases. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, the proxy statement, fourth-quarter results and peer data. Top risk: shareholder returns that exceed free cash flow.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
